name: Crossplay (gender-bending cosplay)

card.summary: Cosplaying a character of a different gender, using wigs, makeup, costume and body styling to transform one's look into the character's.
card.note: Community reception varies; some conventions and critics have objected.

quick.overview:
Crossplay is cosplay in which a person dresses as a character of another gender. It relies on the same appearance toolkit as cosplay generally: wigs, makeup, costume construction and posture or mannerisms, so that the person looks like the chosen character.

It began in anime convention circles and is now widespread. Female-to-male crossplay is more common in most cosplay countries, while male-to-female crossplay is relatively more common outside Japan.
quick.how: Crossplayers choose a character, often with androgynous or bishōnen features, and use styled wigs, makeup that reshapes features, costume tailoring and sometimes shaved eyebrows or colored lenses. Many also practice the character's mannerisms and voice, which distinguishes crossplay from simple gender-swapped costume design.
quick.risks: Risks are mainly social: some crossplayers report homophobic comments or unwanted touching at events, and in 2023 TFcon banned crossplay after Florida's drag law. Makeup and lens use carry ordinary cosmetic cautions.

lead: Crossplay, a blend of 'cross-dressing' and 'cosplay', is cosplay of a character of another gender. It is related to Rule 63 or genderbend cosplay, but crossplayers typically adopt the other gender's mannerisms fully rather than choosing a few traits.[1]

Crossplay began on the anime convention circuit and has spread beyond anime. Wikipedia reports that female-to-male crossplay is much more common in most cosplay countries, helped by bishōnen characters whose delicate features make them easier to portray, while male-to-female crossplay is more common outside Japan.[1]

Cosplay appearance craft includes wigs, makeup to simulate skin tone, colored and circle lenses, body paint and eyebrow shaving; crossplayers apply these skills to reshape the face and silhouette toward a character.[2]

chain: Wig, makeup and costume match the character
Face and silhouette shift toward the character's look
angle.text: People use crossplay to change their look dramatically with wigs, contouring, costume tailoring and body language, turning cosmetic skills into a recognizable character.

paras: Crossplay is portraying a character of a different gender. Wikipedia describes the crossplayer as fully immersed in the codes of another gender, in contrast to Rule 63 cosplay.[1] Cosplay overall holds that anyone can portray anyone, and gender-bending is part of that ethos.[2]

Cosplayers use wigs, makeup, colored contact lenses (including circle lenses), temporary tattoos and body paint; shaving eyebrows is common.[2] The niche animegao kigurumi style uses zentai bodysuits and stylized masks.[2]

Male cosplayers portraying female characters have reported discrimination including homophobic comments and unwanted touching.[2] Anti-LGBTQ activists have criticized crossplay and compared it to drag, and in 2023 TFcon banned crossplay after Florida passed an anti-drag law, offering refunds.[1]

timeline.event: Term 'cosplay' coined in Japan's My Anime magazine.[2]
TFcon bans crossplay after Florida anti-drag law.[1]
